medicare_sample.name: Medicare (sample)
medicare_sample.note: Appeal levels, deadlines and decision times are official CMS rules (each level names its page). The contractor names, addresses and fax numbers are made up for the demo; a real appeal goes to the address on the real notice.

levels.name: Redetermination
levels.how_to_file: In writing: form CMS-20027, or a written request that gives the beneficiary name, the Medicare number, the specific services or items, the specific dates of service, the name of the party or the party's representative, and why the appellant disagrees.

rule.text: File within 120 days of receiving the initial determination. Medicare presumes the notice was received 5 calendar days after the date on it. The MAC generally decides within 60 days of receiving the request. No minimum amount is needed.
quotes: has 120 days from the date of receipt of the initial claim determination to file a redetermination request
is presumed to be received 5 calendar days after the date of the notice
within 60 days of receipt of the request for redetermination
A minimum monetary threshold on the claim is not required to request a redetermination.

levels.name: Reconsideration
levels.how_to_file: Form CMS-20033 or a written request, sent with a copy of the redetermination notice to the QIC. The redetermination notice gives the instructions.

rule.text: File within 180 days of receiving the redetermination decision, presumed received 5 days after the date on the notice. The QIC generally decides within 60 days. Send all evidence now: documents not sent at this level may be excluded at later levels unless there is good cause.
quotes: has 180 days from the date of receipt of the redetermination decision to file a reconsideration request.
is presumed to be received 5 days after the date on the notice
Generally, the QIC will send this decision to all parties within 60 days of receipt of the request for reconsideration.
Any documentation not submitted at the reconsideration level may be excluded from consideration
A minimum monetary threshold is not required to request a reconsideration.

levels.name: Hearing by an Administrative Law Judge (OMHA)
levels.letter_title: Request for an Administrative Law Judge Hearing
levels.decided_by: Office of Medicare Hearings and Appeals (OMHA)
levels.how_to_file: By mail or through the OMHA e-Appeal Portal. The QIC's reconsideration decision letter gives full details.

rule.text: File with OMHA within 60 days of receiving the reconsideration decision, presumed received 5 days after the date of the notice. For 2026 the amount in controversy must be at least $200. OMHA must generally decide within 90 days of receiving the request.
quotes: A request for an ALJ hearing must be filed with OMHA within 60 days of receipt of the reconsideration decision.
The date of receipt of the reconsideration decision is presumed to be 5 days after the date of the decision notice, unless there is evidence to the contrary.
For calendar year 2026 the amount in controversy is $200.

lines: Office of Medicare Hearings and Appeals (OMHA)
Use the mailing address or e-Appeal Portal named in the QIC decision letter

levels.name: Review by the Medicare Appeals Council
levels.letter_title: Request for Review by the Medicare Appeals Council

deadline.counted_from: receipt of the OMHA decision or dismissal

rule.text: File within 60 days of receiving OMHA's decision or dismissal, presumed received 5 days after its date. There is no minimum amount. The Council generally has 90 days.
quotes: within 60 days of receipt of the notice of OMHA's decision or dismissal.
no requirement regarding the amount of money in controversy

lines: Use the address named in the OMHA decision

levels.name: Judicial review in federal district court
levels.how_to_file: A lawyer files in court. Not done by our workers.

rule.text: File within 60 days after receiving the Council's decision, presumed received 5 days after its date. For 2026 the amount in controversy must be at least $1,960.
quotes: within 60 calendar days after the date it receives notice of the Council's decision.
For calendar year 2026, the amount in controversy threshold is $1,960.

medicare_rules.title: What a written redetermination request must include
medicare_rules.text: A redetermination must be requested in writing, on form CMS-20027 or in a letter that gives: the beneficiary name; the Medicare number; the specific services or items; the specific dates of service; the name of the party or the party's representative; and why the appellant disagrees with the decision.
quotes: Beneficiary name
Medicare number
Specific service(s) and/or item(s) for which a redetermination is being requested
Specific date(s) of service
Name of the party, or the representative of the party
An explanation of why the appellant disagrees with the contractor's determination

medicare_rules.title: Appointing a representative (CMS-1696)
medicare_rules.text: Form CMS-1696 appoints a representative to act for a party on a claim or appeal. It is valid for one year from the date both the party and the representative sign it. Fee approval is not required when the party being represented is a provider or supplier. A MAC may dismiss a redetermination request when the representative is not appointed properly.
quotes: Use this form to appoint a representative to act on your behalf for your claim, appeal, grievance or request.
considered valid for one year from the date this form is signed by both.
the appellant being represented is a provider or supplier.
The representative is not appointed properly
medicare_rules.demo_use: Our policy in the demo: when we file an appeal for a practice as its appointed representative, the letter says so and a signed CMS-1696 goes with it. When the practice signs and files the appeal itself, no form is needed. Melvin confirms this policy with the lawyer before real use.

medicare_rules.title: Good cause for late filing
medicare_rules.text: A late appeal can be accepted only with good cause, for example: a serious illness, a death or serious illness in the immediate family, records destroyed by a fire or other disaster, wrong or incomplete information from the contractor about when and how to appeal, or never receiving the notice. To ask, explain why the appeal is late, send that explanation with the appeal, and include any evidence.
quotes: Important records were destroyed or damaged by fire or other event, like a hurricane, earthquake or flood
The contractor or appeals reviewer gave you incorrect or incomplete information about when and how to file an appeal
You didn't get notice of the determination or decision

medicare_rules.title: Clerical errors go to a reopening, not an appeal
medicare_rules.text: Clerical errors, including minor errors and omissions, are handled as reopenings. A reopening can be asked for within 1 year of the initial determination for any reason. If a redetermination request turns out to be only a minor error or omission, the contractor processes it as a reopening.
quotes: Clerical errors (which include minor errors and omissions) shall be treated as reopenings
within 1 year from the date of the initial determination or redetermination for any reason
